summary: Tested Agenda→Consulta unified flow end-to-end. 7/8 backend tests passed and full frontend UI flow works: login, navigate to /agenda, click 'Iniciar Atendimento' navigates to /atendimento/agenda/{id}, timer counts up, patient Maria Silva pre-filled, Botox pre-selected, all 5 tabs present (Anamnese, Procedimento, Fotos, Produtos, Orçamento), Finalizar button present, receipt PDF endpoint returns valid application/pdf, GET /api/appointments/{id} works (200 + 404), POST /medical-records with appointment_id correctly marks the appointment as 'completed' and creates a finance income transaction. ONE CRITICAL BUG: stock deduction silently fails — botox quantity NOT reduced after consultation.

critical.issue: Stock NOT deducted for products_used. After creating a record with products_used=[{product_id, quantity:50}], the product quantity in /api/products remains unchanged (still 200, expected 150). Root cause: server.py:849 queries `db.products.find_one({"id": product_id})` and line 852-855 updates `{"id": product_id}`, but products are stored in MongoDB with the key `qr_code_id`, not `id` (see /api/products GET which maps qr_code_id→id only on response). Lookup returns None, so the $inc update is never executed and no movement record is created. Movement integration broken in same way.

action_items: Fix server.py create_medical_record stock deduction: replace `db.products.find_one({"id": product_id})` with `db.products.find_one({"qr_code_id": product_id})` and the corresponding update_one filter on line 852-855. Same for movement.product_name lookup. After the fix, rerun test_consultation_flow.py — test_create_medical_record_full_flow should pass.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py uses inconsistent identifiers for products: storage uses `qr_code_id` but reads/writes elsewhere expect `id`. This is a footgun — any feature querying products by id will silently fail. Recommend either storing `id` field (= qr_code_id) at write time in /api/products POST/PUT, or auditing every db.products.find_one/update_one call for the right filter.
Bare `except:` in get_current_user (line 551) hides real errors. Use `except Exception as e` and log.
server.py is very large (~3500+ lines based on truncation) — consider splitting into routers (auth, agenda, prontuario, financeiro, etc.) for maintainability.

The bug is purely in stock integration.
rca of the issue: Bug: products_used does not decrement stock. RCA: POST /api/medical-records iterates products_used and calls `db.products.find_one({'id': product_id})` + `db.products.update_one({'id': product_id}, {'$inc': {'quantity': -qty}})`. However products are inserted with `qr_code_id` (server.py POST /products line 1251) and never receive an `id` field in MongoDB. GET /api/products synthesizes `p['id'] = p['qr_code_id']` only in the response. So when frontend POSTs products_used with the product 'id' it received, the backend lookup misses. Reproduction: POST /api/medical-records with products_used=[{product_id: <botox_id>, quantity: 50}] → /api/products botox quantity stays 200. Mitigation: change both filters in create_medical_record to use `qr_code_id`. Long-term: persist `id` alongside `qr_code_id` on product create/update so every collection uses a uniform key.
